title: Problems and Countermeasures in Natural Language Processing Evaluation

bias_targets.methodology: The paper reviews the evaluation of gender bias in coreference resolution systems using datasets like Winogender, discussing how models may rely on spurious gender-occupation stereotypes found in training data (e.g., associating 'rescuer' with male pronouns).

The paper addresses the limitation of evaluations focused solely on high-resource languages (specifically English) and reviews the development of multilingual benchmarks (such as XTREME and XGLUE) designed to evaluate model performance across diverse language families and low-resource languages.

The paper analyzes various forms of statistical bias and spurious correlations in datasets, such as answer distribution bias, irrelevant cue bias (heuristic adoption), and type distribution bias, which allow models to achieve high scores without true language understanding.
